question.text: The percentage price movement caused by an order of a particular size from the average of the best bid and offer price is called:

explanation.text: The Logic: Impact cost is defined as the percentage price movement caused by an order of a particular size from the average of the best bid and offer price. Lower impact cost implies higher liquidity in the stock. The Trap: Spread cost refers to the bid-ask spread itself and does not factor in order size. Tracking error and transaction tax are unrelated concepts. Note: Impact cost is an order-size-sensitive liquidity measure — the same stock can have a low impact cost for small orders and a high impact cost for large orders.
